items.t: Janus Henderson CEO on Going Private, M&A Deals
items.d: Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj said the firm is energized by its move to private ownership and is using the flexibility to invest in people, technology including AI, new products and client service. He said quarterly earnings pressures had constrained those investments, despite the firm’s growth as a public company. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Vanguard CIO Greg Davis on Market, Inflation Outlook
items.d: Vanguard President and CIO Greg Davis said the CPI report was one data point for markets and the Federal Reserve to assess, while noting inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target and the Fed still has work to do. Davis said Vanguard generally expects one to two rate hikes over the coming months, depending on incoming data. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers
items.d: Startup Ambrosia Energy will build a massive factory to crank out batteries to augment solar panels, creating a round-the-clock clean power plant.
items.fullText: Ambrosia Energy has begun work on a massive, 10 gigawatt-hour battery factory near Austin, Texas, co-founder and CEO Ben Longmier announced onstage Tuesday at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco. “That allows us to build about a 300 megawatt power plant per year out at our field sites,” he said. The factory will occupy 150,000 square feet, and Longmier said that Ambrosia plans to reach full production in two to three years. The startup emerged from stealth in June to build power plants for data centers at a cost of $100 per megawatt hour. Longmier and his co-founder, Sara Spangelo, had settled on solar plus batteries as the cheapest option that’s the fastest to deploy. Solar panels power the load during the day and charge the batteries, which discharge at night and on cloudy days to keep the data center operating round the clock. Longmier and Spangelo previously founded the satellite constellation startup Swarm, which they sold to SpaceX. Ambrosia is also beginning work on its first commercial power plant in West Texas later this year, Longmier said. The facility will pair 300 megawatts of solar panels with 660 megawatt-hours of batteries to deliver 30 megawatts of continuous power, with a goal of 99.3% uptime. Even with “overbuilding” solar and batteries to deliver continuous uptime, Longmier said the company can be profitable at $100 per megawatt-hour, making it competitive with natural gas turbines that many hyperscalers are planning to use to power their data centers. Sections of Ambrosia’s first pilot-scale power plant have been operating continuously for more than 100 days, Longmier said. The pilot is capable of generating 200 kilowatts of electricity 24/7. To hit its cost targets, Ambrosia has been finding ways to simplify its components, including solar mounts and battery packs. items.t: Prismm helps banks keep inherited money in-house
items.d: With Prismm, account holders can give designated family members access to their accounts and documents ahead of time.
items.fullText: Meet Prismm , a startup that helps banks keep families’ money in-house after an account holder dies. It does this by building beneficiary and estate planning into accounts from day one, which makes the transfer of assets to heirs less complicated. Prismm is presenting its mission today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 . Prismm was founded in 2020 by sisters Martha Underwood and Shella Sylla, who each have decades of experience in banking and finance. The pair came up with the idea for Prismm based on their own experience of seeing firsthand how difficult it can be to manage a family’s affairs in an emergency. Their father was hospitalized in 2017 after he fell while helping clear a tree from a neighbor’s roof following Hurricane Irma in Miami. Their mother, who had always relied on him to handle the family’s finances and paperwork, didn’t know where all the important documents and financial information were, and neither did they. Their father recovered, but the experience of not knowing how to access critical information stuck with them. That was the starting point for Prismm, but the idea really took shape three years later, when Underwood was working at a bank during the COVID-19 pandemic. She saw families come in after a loved one had died, scrambling to find accounts, understand bills, and figure out how to support the surviving spouse. Image Credits: Prismm “That’s when it hit us that this is an infrastructure problem, and as I started to dig deeper, we’ve created all of these platforms for wealth growth and tracking, but almost nothing for transition,” Underwood said in an interview with TechCrunch. “It’s still very much all manual. items.t: NTangible bets it can predict how athletes will perform under pressure
items.d: NTangible is building an analytics platform for collegiate sports organizations and other clubs to measure an athlete's "clutch" factor.
items.fullText: When collegiate sports programs recruit athletes, they can measure concrete metrics like a player’s sprint speed, throwing velocity, and physical strength. But there has never been a clear way to quantify the mental aspects of sports — how well will this athlete perform in high-pressure situations? Will they stay calm, focus, and give it their best shot? Or will they panic in the spotlight and mess up? NTangible co-founder and CEO Dan Connerty thinks he’s unlocked the secret to measuring if a player will execute in the most important moments. “We really wanted to hyper focus on this idea of clutch performance,” Connerty, a professional baseball player turned sports-tech entrepreneur, told TechCrunch. “Cognitive [science] itself is just this black box that nobody’s wanted to touch, because nobody’s had the ability to measure it accurately prior.” Alongside psychologist Dr. Ed Levine, a professor emeritus at the University of South Florida, Connerty developed a psychological assessment that he says can predict how likely an athlete is to perform under pressure. The Clutch Factor assessment is inspired by the Thematic Apperception Test, a psychological examination in which people are presented with photos of ambiguous situations and describe what they see happening, who they imagine themselves to be in the scene, and what they think might happen next. Image Credits: NTangible “There’s no right or wrong answers,” Connerty said. “The key words that you use, the way in which you use those words, and the semantic phrasing associated with it get scored against the neurolinguistic scoring guide that psychologists created, and it shoots out your clutch factor score.” The score is between 0 and 1,000 and, according to Connerty, an athlete who scores over a 750 is twice as likely to commit to a Division I school. “What we’ve been able to do is leverage this analysis, where we can sho

Musk put the responsibility for the restrictions on President Donald Trump’s shoulders on social media , saying the military version of Starlink, called Starshield, is owned and controlled by the U.S. government. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said. A spokesperson for President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News that the limitations remained in place late Wednesday. Facing pressure from Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried that Washington could cut off battlefield support to try to force it into concessions at the negotiating table. Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence-sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem UK organizations across healthcare, finance, local government and climate science are putting NVIDIA AI to work. October 13, 2026 by Anthony Hills 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work — and the scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems. NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS.
